title: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ditches the Old Playbook With Passport-Sized Redesign
excerpt: Samsung's new foldable trades its tall, boxy form factor for a wider, squatter design that weighs just 201 grams and starts at $1,899 in the US and ₹1,79,999 in India.
body:
• Samsung has completely redesigned the Z Fold 8 with a compact, passport-style form factor — wider and squatter than any previous Fold — weighing just 201 grams.
  • The 7.8-inch inner display features a tablet-friendly 4:3 aspect ratio and Samsung's new Flex Titanium technology that virtually eliminates the visible crease.
  • A dual 50MP camera setup replaces the triple-camera system of its predecessor, dropping the dedicated zoom lens to the pricier Fold 8 Ultra.
  • Available for pre-order in India from ₹1,79,999 ($1,899 in the US), with shipments starting August 4 and an ₹9,000 instant bank discount for pre-orders.

A Completely New Shape

Forget everything you knew about Samsung's book-style foldables. The Galaxy Z Fold 8, launched at Samsung's Unpacked event on July 22, 2026, abandons the tall, narrow cover screen and boxy interior that defined every Fold from the original through last year's Z Fold 7. In its place is a shorter, wider device that Samsung pitches as "passport-sized" — and after a week of real-world use, reviewers say the comparison is apt.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=3vvJeRHe3sk

The cover screen shrinks to 5.5 inches with a 16:10 aspect ratio, while the inner foldable panel stretches to 7.8 inches in a near-square 4:3 layout. The result, according to Trusted Reviews, is a foldable that works equally well for one-handed messaging on the outside and full-screen video or social media browsing on the inside.

"After a week of everyday use, the wider, squatter Z Fold 8 has changed how I think a book-style foldable should feel."

— Trusted Reviews

At 201 grams, the Z Fold 8 is Samsung's lightest book-style foldable ever — lighter, in fact, than the company's own Galaxy S26 Ultra slab phone. It slips into pockets without the awkward bulk that has dogged previous Fold models.

Display and Crease Improvements

Samsung's new Flex Titanium technology is the engineering headline here. Two layers embedded in the inner folding panel reduce the crease to near-invisibility when viewed head-on and make the plastic screen feel noticeably sturdier under the finger. Combined with the same anti-reflective coating used on the Galaxy S26 Ultra, the inner display sheds the plastic sheen that has long been a foldable complaint.

Both screens run Dynamic AMOLED 2X panels with 120Hz LTPO refresh rates and peak brightness of 3,000 nits. The cover screen, despite its smaller size, matches the inner panel in specs and is better suited to gaming and 16:9 video than the narrow cover screens of earlier Folds.

Under the Hood

Powering the Z Fold 8 is Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy, the same chip found in the Galaxy S26 Ultra. It ships with either 12GB or 16GB of RAM and storage options of 256GB, 512GB, or 1TB.

Day-to-day performance is snappy — apps open instantly, One UI 9 (built on Android 17) feels fluid, and the phone handles routine multitasking without issue. But the Fold 8's slimmer chassis limits sustained performance under heavy loads. Trusted Reviews noted occasional stutters during 4K video editing and intensive gaming, and Samsung appears to have blocked standard benchmarking apps on the device, a move the reviewer called unusual for Samsung.

Samsung promises seven years of OS upgrades and security patches, making the Z Fold 8 the first phone to ship with Android 17 out of the box, beating Google's upcoming Pixel 11 range by several weeks.

Camera Compromises

This is where the Z Fold 8 makes its biggest trade-off. The triple-camera system from last year's Z Fold 7 — headlined by a 200MP main sensor and dedicated telephoto lens — has been replaced by a simpler dual 50MP setup with a main and ultrawide camera. There is no dedicated zoom lens; digital cropping beyond 2-3x quickly degrades image quality.

For everyday shooting and social media, the cameras perform well, producing Samsung's characteristically vibrant images with solid detail. Low-light performance is acceptable thanks to the main camera's f/1.8 aperture, though the smaller 1/1.57-inch sensor cannot match top-end camera phones. If photography is a priority, Samsung steers buyers toward the Z Fold 8 Ultra, which retains the 200MP main sensor and 10MP telephoto with 3x optical zoom.

Battery and Charging

The 4,800mAh battery is only 200mAh smaller than the Fold 8 Ultra's and lasted through 16-18 hour days with around six hours of mixed screen time in reviewer testing, typically ending the day at 5-10%. The 45W wired charging fills the battery from zero to 67% in 30 minutes and completes a full charge in 68 minutes. Wireless charging tops out at 20W.

Pricing and Availability in India

Samsung has priced the Galaxy Z Fold 8 in India starting at ₹1,79,999 for the 12GB/256GB base variant, rising to ₹1,99,999 for 512GB and ₹2,39,999 for the 1TB model. In the US, the base model retails at $1,899 and £1,699 in the UK. Pre-orders are live now, with Samsung offering an ₹9,000 instant bank discount and up to nine months of no-cost EMI. Shipments in India begin August 4, according to SamMobile, with retail availability starting August 8.

The device comes in Graphite, Cream, Lavender, and Pistachio (the last one exclusive to Samsung's own store).

What to Watch For

Samsung has split its foldable lineup into two distinct identities: the Z Fold 8 for content consumption and everyday use, and the Z Fold 8 Ultra for productivity power users. Early reviews call the standard Fold 8 the most enjoyable Samsung foldable in years, but the camera downgrade and sustained performance limitations may give some buyers pause. With competitors like Oppo and Honor pushing larger batteries and better camera systems in their foldables, Samsung's bet on form factor alone will face a real test once the phones hit shelves next week.
